mainTopic: Why כהנים and לוים are exempt from בכורה laws: the קל וחומר of אביי and רבא, the challenges of רב ספרא, and the group link of all לוים.
overview: The משנה said that כהנים and לוים are exempt from the laws of the firstborn because of a קל וחומר: if they exempted the firstborns of ישראל in the מדבר, they should surely exempt their own. The גמרא objects that, according to the פסוק, people exempted people and animals exempted animals. אביי answers that the משנה is about the לוים's animals. רבא rejects this from the משנה's wording and from the rule that they still owe בכור בהמה טהורה. רבא explains instead that the לוים exempted themselves, and a פסוק that links the human firstborn to the donkey firstborn extends this exemption to their donkeys. רב ספרא then challenges both explanations: what about a לוי with no sheep, a לוי under a month old, a לויה's son, and אהרן, who was not counted? The גמרא answers that firstborn status follows the mother's womb ('פטר רחם'), and that the word 'הלוים' links all לוים together as one group. Finally, רבי יהושע בן לוי shows that כהנים are called 'לוים' in twenty-four places, so אהרן is included too.

steps.title: Did the Levites themselves exempt the animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. People exempted people and animals exempted animals, so the לוים did not personally exempt everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Did THEY exempt? A person exempted a person, and an animal exempted an animal, as it is written: 'Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the children of Israel, and the animal of the Levites in place of their animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the משנה's claim that the כהנים and לוים themselves exempted the firstborns of ישראל in the desert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes two separate exchanges. The לוים took the place of the human firstborns, and the לוים's animals took the place of ישראל's firstborn animals. So the משנה's wording, 'they exempted,' cannot cover the animal firstborns (such as פטר חמור), because those were exempted by animals, not by people.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that analyzes the משנה
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
In place of / in exchange for

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not denying that the desert exchange happened. It is only questioning WHO exempted the animal firstborns: the לוים themselves, or their animals.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Did they exempt?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical challenge to the משנה's wording

phrases.english: A person — a person exempted,
phrases.notes: The Levites exempted the human firstborns

phrases.english: an animal — an animal exempted,
phrases.notes: The Levites' animals exempted ישראל's animals

phrases.english: as it is written: 'Take the Levites
in place of the firstborn among the children of Israel
and the animal of the Levites in place of their animal'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the כהנים and לוים exempted ישראל's firstborns.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows that animals exempted animals, so the people could not have exempted the animal firstborns.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה is about the Levites' own animals
steps.stepSummary: אביי reinterprets the משנה: the animals of the כהנים and לוים are exempt, through a קל וחומר based on their animals having exempted ישראל's animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the משנה means. The כהנים and לוים are exempt regarding their animals by a קל וחומר: if the animals of the לוים cancelled the firstborn status of ישראל's animals in the desert, it is only logical that they should cancel the status of their own animals.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by rereading the משנה so that the קל וחומר is about animals exempting animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading fits the פסוק, since animals exempted animals. The reasoning runs as follows: if the לוים's animals were powerful enough to remove someone else's firstborn status, they can surely remove the status of the לוים's own firstborn animals.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introduces a reinterpretation)
A fortiori argument (from a weaker case to a stronger one)

phrases.english: Abaye said, this is what it is saying:
priests and Levites are exempt regarding their animals
from an a fortiori argument —
if the animals of the Levites cancelled
the status of the animals of Israel in the desert,

phrases.aramaic: דִּין הוּא שֶׁתַּפְקִיעַ אֶת שֶׁל עַצְמָן.
phrases.english: it is logical that they should cancel that of their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1 by reinterpreting the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה meant that the people themselves exempted all the firstborns.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means that the כהנים' and לוים' animals are exempt, by a קל וחומר from their animals.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה says 'they' exempted
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the משנה's wording explicitly says the people ('they') exempted, not their animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But the משנה teaches 'THEY exempted'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer by pointing to the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reading makes the animals the subject of the exemption. The משנה, however, says 'פטרו,' meaning the כהנים and לוים themselves. So אביי's reading does not match the text.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (refers to the משנה's wording)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But it teaches 'they exempted' — them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא ״פָּטְרוּ״ אִינְהוּ קָתָנֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the animals are the subject of the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's verb 'פטרו' refers to the people, not to their animals.

steps.title: רבא's second objection: then kosher firstborns should be exempt too
steps.stepSummary: If אביי's קל וחומר were valid, it would also exempt the כהנים and לוים from בכור בהמה טהורה. Yet a משנה says they are exempt only from פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, if this is so, they should be exempt even from the firstborn of a kosher animal! Why then did we learn: They were not exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal, only from redemption of the son and the firstborn donkey?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second, stronger objection: אביי's logic proves too much, because it contradicts another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the desert, the לוים's animals stood in place of ישראל's animals in general. So אביי's קל וחומר should exempt all of the לוים's firstborn animals, including kosher ones. But the משנה (on 13a) rules that the כהנים and לוים still owe בכור בהמה טהורה. Therefore the קל וחומר cannot be about animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Why then did we learn (in a משנה)?

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא asks how 'they' could exempt animals (step 1). אביי says the משנה is about their animals (step 2). רבא rejects this on two grounds: the wording says 'they' (step 3), and the logic would wrongly exempt kosher firstborns, contradicting a משנה (step 4).
steps.confusionAlert: The כהנים and לוים are still fully obligated in בכור בהמה טהורה. Their exemption covers only פדיון הבן and פטר חמור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limits of the exemption of כהנים and לוים, and it forces the גמרא to look for another explanation of the משנה.

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it is so,
they should be exempt even from the firstborn of a kosher animal!
Why then did we learn:
they were not exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal,
but only from redemption of the son and the firstborn donkey?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second objection by רבא against אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's קל וחומר based on the לוים's animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The logic would extend to kosher firstborns, which contradicts the explicit ruling of the משנה.

steps.title: רבא's new reading: the Levites exempted themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה means the כהנים and לוים personally exempted themselves. He bases this on a קל וחומר: their holiness cancelled the Israelites' firstborn holiness, so it surely cancels their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what the משנה teaches. The כהנים and לוים exempted themselves through a קל וחומר. If the holiness of the לוים cancelled the holiness of the Israelite firstborns in the מדבר, shouldn't it cancel the holiness of their own firstborns?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the original question on the משנה. He says the משנה's 'they exempted' refers to the people themselves, not their animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, the לוים took the place of the Israelite firstborns and removed their holiness. רבא argues that something strong enough to remove another person's firstborn status is surely strong enough to remove its own. This fits the משנה's wording, which רבא used in step 3 to object to אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier approach and offers a new one)
This is what the משנה is teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two קל וחומרs. אביי's is about animals exempting animals. רבא's is about people (the לוים themselves) exempting people.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is what it teaches:
Priests and Levites exempted themselves
by an a fortiori argument:
If the sanctity of the Levites cancelled
the sanctity of the Israelites' firstborns in the wilderness,
should it not cancel their own?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the problems with אביי's approach (steps 3–4), רבא offers a different reading that fits the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה with a new קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לוים could not have exempted everything, so the משנה must mean their animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The לוים personally exempted themselves, through a קל וחומר from the מדבר.

steps.title: What is the source for exempting their non-kosher animals?
steps.stepSummary: רבא's קל וחומר covers the people. The גמרא asks how we know that their donkeys are exempt from פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for people. From where do we know that their non-kosher animals are exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a gap in רבא's answer and asks for a source for the donkeys. This sets up the next step, which answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts the לוים from both פדיון הבן and פטר חמור. רבא's קל וחומר only explains the human firstborn, so a separate source is needed for the firstborn donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one part)

phrases.english: We have found a source for a person;
for a non-kosher animal, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source to complete רבא's approach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for exempting the לוים's firstborn donkeys from פטר חמור.

steps.title: A verse links the firstborn donkey to the firstborn person
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts the human firstborn and the non-kosher animal firstborn side by side. Whoever is obligated in one is obligated in the other, and whoever is exempt from one is exempt from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'But you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem.' Whoever is obligated in a human firstborn is obligated in a non-kosher animal firstborn. Whoever is not obligated in a human firstborn is not obligated in a non-kosher animal firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. Since the לוים are exempt from פדיון הבן, they are also exempt from פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the two redemptions in one sentence, so the גמרא treats them as one package. The exemption for people that רבא proved automatically carries over to their donkeys.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's approach: the לוים exempted themselves through a קל וחומר, and the פסוק of 'אך פדה תפדה' extends that exemption to their donkeys.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"But you shall surely redeem
the firstborn of man,
and the firstborn of the non-kosher animal you shall redeem"
Whoever is obligated in a human firstborn
is obligated in a non-kosher animal firstborn;
and whoever is not obligated in a human firstborn
is not obligated in a non-kosher animal firstborn.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links the two obligations, so exemption from פדיון הבן brings exemption from פטר חמור.

steps.title: רב ספרא: only a Levite who owned a sheep should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges אביי. If the exemption comes from the לוים's animals, then only a לוי who actually had a sheep to redeem Israelite donkeys should be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to אביי: According to you, who said 'their animals,' a לוי who had a sheep that cancelled the holiness should have his animals' holiness cancelled. A לוי who had no sheep to cancel it should not have it cancelled!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks אביי's animal-based קל וחומר. He shows that it would only work for some לוים, not all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, the לוים's sheep redeemed the Israelites' firstborn donkeys. If that is the source of the exemption, it should depend on whether a particular לוי actually owned a sheep. Yet the exemption applies to every לוי.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Abaye:
According to you, who said 'their animals,'
a Levite who had a sheep
that cancelled the sanctity, let his be cancelled;
one who did not have a sheep
to cancel it, let his not be cancelled!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְאַבָּיֵי: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ בְּהֶמְתָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to challenge אביי's approach from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's קל וחומר based on the לוים's animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the exemption depends on animals that redeemed, it should be limited to לוים who actually owned such animals.

steps.title: רב ספרא: only Levites at least a month old should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges both אביי and רבא. Only לוים who were counted from one month old replaced the firstborns, so younger לוים should not be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both according to you and according to רבא: a לוי who was a month old, who did cancel the holiness, should have his own holiness cancelled. One less than a month old, who did not cancel it, should not have his cancelled!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא raises a second challenge that hits both אביי and רבא. The exemption should only cover לוים who actually took part in the exchange in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוים were counted from one month and up (במדבר ג:טו), and only those counted replaced the Israelite firstborns. Both explanations agree that the לוים exempted themselves from personal בכור status through their role in the מדבר. So a לוי under a month old, who had no role, should still need פדיון הבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Both according to you and according to רבא

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge threatens the basic idea that the לוים's role in the מדבר is the source of their exemption, whether through their animals or through themselves.

phrases.english: Both according to you and according to Rava:
one a month old, who cancelled the sanctity, let his be cancelled;
one less than a month old, who did not cancel it,
let his not be cancelled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge from רב ספרא that now covers both approaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both אביי's and רבא's קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only לוים aged a month or more replaced the firstborns, so the exemption should not apply to younger לוים.

steps.title: A Levite woman's firstborn son should not be exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא continues: women were not counted in the exchange, so a לויה's son should keep his firstborn holiness. Yet רב אדא בר אהבה rules that he is exempt from the five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a Levite woman, should [her son's firstborn holiness] not be cancelled? Then why did רב אדא בר אהבה say: a Levite woman who gave birth, her son is exempt from the five סלעים?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא raises another challenge. If the exemption comes only from the exchange, a Levite woman (who was never counted) should not pass on any exemption. But a known ruling says her son is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only male לוים were counted and swapped for the Israelite firstborns. So under אביי and רבא's reasoning, a לויה never had her holiness used in the exchange, and her son's firstborn holiness should remain. רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling that her son is exempt from פדיון הבן contradicts this.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman from the tribe of לוי (a Levite's daughter)
The five silver coins paid to a כהן for פדיון הבן

steps.confusionAlert: The case is a לויה married to a ישראל. Normally a child's tribe follows the father, so the son is a ישראל. That is exactly why his exemption is surprising.

phrases.english: A Levite woman, should [her son's firstborn holiness] not be cancelled?
phrases.notes: Women were not counted in the exchange.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Why then did Rav Adda bar Ahava say:
A Levite woman who gave birth,
her son is exempt from the five sela coins?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְוִיָּה לָא תַּיפְקַע? אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge in רב ספרא's series, after the sheep challenge (step 8) and the one-month challenge (step 9).
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי and רבא's claim that the exemption comes from the exchange in the מדבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Women were not part of the exchange, so the theory predicts that a לויה's son is obligated. רב אדא בר אהבה rules that he is exempt.

steps.title: Firstborn status depends on the mother's womb
steps.stepSummary: The לויה problem is answered using מר בריה דרב יוסף in the name of רבא: the תורה ties firstborn status to the womb, so the mother's Levite status is what counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. It follows מר son of רב יוסף in the name of רבא, who said: 'Opening of the womb' means the תורה made it depend on the opening of the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers only the last challenge, about the לויה. Since the תורה calls a firstborn 'פטר רחם', the mother is the deciding factor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'פטר רחם' show that firstborn status is defined through the mother's womb, not the father. So if the mother is a לויה, her Levite standing governs, and the son is exempt even though his father is a ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The opening of the womb': the Torah's term for a firstborn
The Merciful One (the Torah) made it depend on

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic rule that a לויה's firstborn son needs no פדיון הבן, even if his father is a ישראל.

phrases.english: This is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: as in the statement of Mar son of Rav Yosef in the name of Rava,
who said: 'Opening of the womb'
The Merciful One made it depend on the opening of the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, כִּדְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the לויה challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source reading: firstborn status is defined by the womb
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son follows his Israelite father, so he should be a regular obligated בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'פטר רחם' ties firstborn status to the mother, so a לויה's son is exempt.

steps.title: אהרן was not counted, so his firstborn status should remain
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges again: a ברייתא says the dots over 'אהרן' in במדבר show he was not part of the count of לוים. So his firstborn holiness should not have been cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אהרן, who was not in that count, should not have his status cancelled! As it was taught: Why are there dots over 'אהרן' in the book of במדבר? To show that he was not in that count.
steps.whatsHappening: Another challenge to the exchange theory. אהרן was not among the counted לוים, so by that reasoning his own firstborn holiness should still apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא said that a לוי's holiness cancelled firstborn holiness because the לוים were swapped for the firstborns. The ברייתא, based on the dots over 'אהרן' (במדבר ג:לט), shows that אהרן was left out of that count. So the swap could not have affected him.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
Dotted: marked with dots above the letters in the ספר תורה
'The book of the counts', meaning ספר במדבר

phrases.english: And Aaron, who was not in that count,
should not be cancelled!
As it was taught: Why are there dots over 'Aaron'
in the book of Numbers?
To show that he was not in that count.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּאוֹתוֹ מִנְיָן לָא לַיפְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in רב ספרא's series, similar to the one-month challenge: someone outside the count should not be exempt.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exchange theory of אביי and רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא proves that אהרן was outside the count, so the exchange should not have cancelled his own firstborn holiness.

steps.title: All the לוים are linked together as one group
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'הלוים', which teaches a הקש: all לוים are compared to one another. So even לוים outside the count, like אהרן, share the exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'The Levites.' All the Levites were compared to one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'הלוים' (במדבר ג:מה) makes all לוים equal. Whatever applies to the counted לוים applies to every לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption does not depend on each individual being personally counted or swapped. Because the תורה groups all לוים together, the uncounted ones (אהרן, and also those not yet a month old) are included.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says (introducing a proof from a פסוק)
They were compared / linked (by a הקש)
A Torah comparison that applies the law of one thing to another

steps.whatToRemember: The exemption of לוים from firstborn laws is a group status. A לויה's son is exempt because of 'פטר רחם' (the mother decides), and uncounted לוים like אהרן are exempt because 'הלוים' links all לוים together.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say that אהרן was secretly counted. It accepts that he was left out, but says the group link makes that irrelevant.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'The Levites,'
all the Levites were compared to one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: הַלְוִיִּם, הוּקְשׁוּ כׇּל הַלְוִיִּם זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אהרן challenge, and by its logic also the earlier challenge about לוים under a month old. The גמרא does not explicitly answer the sheep challenge, which was aimed only at אביי's reading that רבא had already rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הקש from a פסוק that makes all לוים one group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only לוים who were personally counted and swapped lost their firstborn holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: All לוים are linked, so even uncounted ones like אהרן are exempt.

steps.title: How do we know priests are included?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that כהנים are included in the לוים's exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that priests are included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question. It is setting up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הקש of 'הלוים' compares all לוים to each other. But אהרן was a כהן, not a regular לוי. So we still need a source that כהנים count as part of 'לוים' in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: Priests, from where do we know [they are included]?
phrases.notes: Refers back to אהרן, who was a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the הקש from Step 13 by asking how כהנים fit inside the word 'לוים'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source showing that כהנים are called לוים, so the הקש can apply to אהרן.

steps.title: Priests are called Levites in twenty-four places
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי shows that the פסוקים call כהנים 'לוים' in twenty-four places, for example 'והכהנים הלוים בני צדוק'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: In twenty-four places the priests are called 'Levites', and this is one of them: 'But the priests the Levites, the sons of צדוק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי. He shows that the תנ"ך often calls כהנים by the name 'לוים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוקים themselves call כהנים 'לוים', then כהנים are part of the group named 'הלוים'. So the הקש that compares all לוים also covers אהרן. That is why his firstborn holiness was cancelled even though he was not counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Levites, members of the tribe of לוי
The sons of צדוק, a family of כהנים (from יחזקאל 44:15)

steps.whatToRemember: כהנים are called 'לוים' in twenty-four places. So they are part of the 'הלוים' הקש, and that is why even אהרן, who was not counted, lost his firstborn holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the last gap in the explanation of how אהרן was exempt. It also shows a general rule: כהנים are a subgroup of לוים, so a law said about לוים can include them.

phrases.english: It is like [the teaching of] Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
In twenty-four places
the priests are called 'Levites',
and this is one of them:
'But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים call כהנים 'לוים' in twenty-four places, such as 'והכהנים הלוים בני צדוק'. So כהנים are included in the term 'הלוים' and in its הקש.
